language.script_notes: Numerous Indigenous Amazonian languages spoken locally, rarely appearing on formal signage.
false_friends: Brazilian Amazon (same rainforest biome, shares much of the border)

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Minimal; the road network is extremely limited in this region.
road_furniture.curb_style: Largely absent — Iquitos itself is famously unreachable by road, accessible only by river or air.

architecture.roof_style: Simple pitched or flat roofs on stilted riverside buildings, built to handle seasonal flooding.
architecture.wall_construction: Stilt houses built above the seasonal flood line are the defining architectural feature along the region's rivers; simple wood-frame construction in jungle towns; Iquitos itself has a distinctive riverboat-and-floating-market culture.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Natural wood tones; brightly painted riverboats and floating structures in Iquitos.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Stilt houses along riverbanks; Iquitos' floating neighborhoods (Belén) and riverboats; jungle lodges deep in the rainforest; motokar (motorcycle taxi) traffic filling Iquitos' streets.

nature.vegetation: Dense lowland equatorial rainforest — among the most biodiverse regions on Earth; seasonally flooded várzea forest along whitewater rivers carrying nutrient-rich Andean sediment; oxbow lakes and meandering river channels.
nature.terrain: Flat lowland Amazon basin, laced with wide, winding rivers (the Amazon's headwaters); no road connection to the rest of Peru in many areas — travel is by river or air.
nature.climate_signature: Hot, humid, and consistently rainy — lush green vegetation year-round, a stark contrast to both the coastal desert and the high Andes.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Motokars (motorcycle taxis) dominate Iquitos' streets given the near-total absence of a road connection to the rest of the country; river boats are the primary long-distance transport.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Very limited official coverage; where present, often Trekker or boat-mounted imagery given the lack of roads.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Among the sparsest coverage in Peru — Iquitos itself has some street-level coverage, but the surrounding rainforest is largely uncovered.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same Amazon rainforest biome, similar stilt-house river architecture and dense vegetation right across the border
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Peru's signage and plates are Spanish-language, right-hand traffic; Brazil's Amazon signage is in Portuguese with its own distinct plate format (Mercosur-style).

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same plate/bollard base style
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The Amazon is dense green lowland rainforest with stilt houses and river transport; the coast is flat barren desert, and the highlands are cold mountainous terrain with Inca-stone architecture — all visually distinct.
